predictions.selection_reason: user-controlled token ID -> creates upload stream -> handles arbitrary file uploads with potential path traversal
predictions.source_summary: Token ID is randomly generated (Random.id()) and not user-controlled. HTTP POST request body data flows directly to the upload stream.
predictions.sink_summary: Creates file upload stream to path '/var/sandstorm/backups/{token._id}' via sandstormBackend.uploadBackup(). FileUploadStream writes uploaded data directly to filesystem.
predictions.guard_summary: No authentication/authorization on upload route. No path traversal validation in uploadBackup implementation. FileUploadStream class implementation details unknown.
predictions.risk_pattern: Unvalidated token ID used directly in filesystem path construction enables path traversal if token ID contains '../' sequences, allowing arbitrary file overwrite.
predictions.context_summary: Route accepts POST requests to /uploadBackup, creates random token, opens upload stream using token ID as path component, streams request data to filesystem.
unresolved_facts: FileUploadStream implementation details and any internal path validation

retrieval_query.sensitive_operation: file upload stream creation using token ID in path
retrieval_query.missing_control: path traversal validation on token ID
retrieval_query.mechanism_keywords: path traversal, directory traversal, arbitrary file write

top_sast_rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-425 forced-browsing direct-request restricted-url protected-route protected-file missing-authorization route endpoint hidden-link
top_sast_rules.remediation: Authorize every protected route and resource on direct access.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.description: Sending network requests with user-controlled data as part of the URL allows for request forgery attacks.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
top_sast_rules.description: Directly sending file data in an outbound network request can indicate unauthorized information disclosure.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find code that may expose sensitive information in error messages, logs, or responses
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper access control checks. Use role-based or attribute-based authorization and validate permissions consistently.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-59 symlink hardlink link-following symbolic-link file-link archive-extraction path-resolution file-overwrite race filesystem
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject unsafe links and verify resolved file targets before access.
